p.i: Τὸ γὰρ τρέφον με, τῆς ἐγὼ κείνῳ Θεόν.
Nam quod me alit, id ego judico Deum

main_text.p: Protagoras, qui ab Athenienfibus capitis condemnatus fuit, eo quod fcripfiffet, περὶ Θεῶν οὔτε εἰσὶν, οὔθ' ὁποῖοί τινες εἰσι, δύναμαί λέγειν. πολλὰ γάρ ἐστι τὰ κωλύοντά με; De Diis neque an sint, neque quales sint habeo dicere. Multa enim sunt quæ me inhibent. Sext. Empir. contra Mathemat. Plures, quod facile possem, adducere mihi animus non est, tum quia id ad rem parum facit, tum quia de multis non satis constat, reverane Deos negaverint, an vero ineptas Gentilium de Diis opiniones & frivolas nænias contemserint oppugnarintque. Quam rem inquirere præterquam quod hujus loci non sit, hominis foret suo otio abutentis,

Quibus si non omnino, proxime tamen accedere videntur duæ non ignobiles Philosophorum sectæ, qui etsi nominatim Deos non proscriberent, eorum tamen omnem claram evidentemq; perceptionem negarunt. Qua in causa primum locum tenent Sceptici, ὃ μᾶλλον εἶναι ἢ μὴ εἶναι Θεὸς λέγοντες, non magis esse, quam non esse Deos afferentes. Sext. Empir. qui etiam Scepticum ea de causa præ reliquis Philosophantium Deosque afferentium sectis constantiæ

page.notes: The Greek lines are printed in italic type and were read with some uncertainty. The Greek epigraph and the Greek phrases in the body are copied as far as they could be read; letters in doubt are not marked individually. The Greek spelling of "ἐγὼ" and "κείνῳ" in the epigraph is uncertain. The left margin strip shows fragments of the neighbouring page and was left out. The numeral "III." is a bare number and is therefore set as a paragraph.
